significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that beliefs carry a recoverable source tag, that "belief-vs-fact errors and source-attribution errors ... coincide with collapse of this provenance separation," and that steering the tag changes source attribution without changing truth-value. This is principally form (ii)—the separable-direction, causal-role, and steering-repair pattern—although the proposed coupling between separation collapse and two related errors adds a modest predictive relation; it would mechanistically constrain explanations of context–memory conflict, a behavior documented in work such as Longpre et al.'s entity-based knowledge-conflict studies. The claim establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, and the branches are distinguishable: a negative result would rule out the stated separable linear-provenance account, though it would not rule out nonlinear or distributed provenance and therefore pays less strongly than the positive branch. Topic-substitution check: merely restating research on internal item beliefs would not justify this score; the source/truth dissociation and selective causal steering are the claim-specific increment, but their consequences remain bounded mainly to provenance-related errors.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "source-misattribution-rate metric," a recoverable "provenance direction," and an intervention that "correct[s] source misattribution without changing the encoded truth-value." The metric is post hoc, but the asserted link that provenance collapse predicts misattribution supplies an ex-ante activation-level warning before the source answer is produced, giving auditors or inference systems an action window. After recalibration on another model, the conclusion predicts the qualitative separation and error coupling but not a quantitative direction or transferable threshold, so much of the intervention must be re-extracted; the hypothesis is phrased broadly about "an LLM," while also acknowledging model-family variation. Topic-substitution check: the topic alone supplies no audit or control handle, whereas this claim specifically hands downstream users a provenance-error predictor and steering knob, satisfying the lead-time route to above-median reach without supporting a universal cross-model law.
